answer: Epochal action hashing forces an agent to publish a hash of its current behavior linked to its prior epoch's hash. The new hash must mirror the pseudorandom output predicted from the past sequence, so a forked clone cannot fabricate a divergent history without breaking the chain. Validators harbor a lightweight verifier that re-runs the exact action schedule from the previous hash, rejecting any mismatch. An attacker pays a lotus of duplicate compute and memory per extra epoch, doubling operational costs per sybil identity.
